name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The only behaviour that can be recovered is clearing two state words and one shared word.

name: copy_longs_to_low_memory
description: Saves the stack pointer, then copies a block of longwords from a fixed source address into low memory with a count-down loop. It calls an unnamed routine afterwards and writes a few more shared words before returning a combined value.

name: copy_longs_with_dma_setup
description: Copies a block of longwords from a fixed source address into low memory with a count-down loop, after storing several shared words and saving the stack pointer. The facts record custom chip register accesses for DMA and interrupt control, which the decompiled body does not show directly.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The only behaviour that can be recovered is clearing two state words and one shared word.

name: flush_pending_bit_flags
description: Writes a constant to a shared word for each set bit of a pending flag byte, then clears that flag. If a second pending flag is set, it calls an unnamed routine and copies five saved words into the shared word before clearing it.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The only behaviour that can be recovered is clearing two state words and one shared word.

name: store_byte_then_call_routine
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into a state byte, then calls an unnamed routine and returns.

name: decode_channel_command_byte
description: Dispatches on the range of an input command byte: special values update the fields of a per-channel record and return, while ordinary values store the note index, reset several record fields and copy a value from a 16-entry lookup table into the record.

name: init_channel_tables_and_pointers
description: Stores the caller's pointer parameters and a base value, then fills a 32-entry word table with a constant and clears a companion table. It finishes by setting four table pointers used by the channel code.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The only behaviour that can be recovered is clearing two state words and one shared word.

name: compare_byte_sets_direction_flag
description: Saves the input's low byte and the byte above it, then sets a flag to one, minus one or zero depending on how the new byte compares with the previously saved byte. The comparison is skipped when the high byte is zero.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The facts list audio period and DMA control register references, but the decompiled body itself only clears state words.

name: reload_countdown_and_poll_flag
description: Decrements a countdown field in a record and, when it goes below zero, reloads it from a shared word. It then repeatedly calls an unnamed routine until a flag byte in the record becomes nonzero.

name: interpret_sequence_command_byte
description: Reads a command byte from a sequence stream and dispatches on its low four bits. Each case updates the record's stream pointer, position counter or flag field, and several cases end the routine while others continue the loop.

name: mark_done_and_advance_counter
description: Sets a state byte to idle and advances a counter pair, resetting it to a stored start value when it reaches its limit. It then calls an unnamed routine and sets a flag byte in the caller's frame.

name: interpret_sequence_with_loop_jump
description: Variant of the sequence command reader that handles one command type by decrementing a repeat counter and jumping into a shared dispatch path. Other command values follow the same low-nibble dispatch and record updates as the neighbouring readers.

name: interpret_sequence_table_jump
description: Sequence command reader that, for one command type, loads a pointer from a table indexed by the command byte and jumps into the shared fetch path. Other command values follow the same low-nibble dispatch as the neighbouring readers.

name: store_byte_and_advance_counter
description: Stores the low byte of a value from the caller's frame into a state byte and increments a position word in the record. It returns immediately afterwards.

name: set_state_byte_to_idle
description: Sets one status byte in the record to the all-ones value and returns. Nothing else in the body is touched.

name: run_sequence_command_loop
description: Loops over command bytes from a sequence stream, advancing the record's position for each one and dispatching on the low four bits. The first command type ends the loop after clearing the state byte, and the other types update counters, pointers or stored values.

name: dispatch_sequence_commands_until_end
description: Reads command bytes from a sequence stream and dispatches on their low four bits, advancing the record's position after each one. Ordinary values continue the loop, while the end-type value clears the state byte and returns.

name: dispatch_sequence_table_command
description: Sequence command reader that first uses the command byte as an index into a pointer table to set the record's stream pointer and state byte, then runs the usual low-nibble dispatch. It calls one unnamed routine during the fetch loop.

name: set_state_byte_to_idle
description: Sets one status byte in the record to the all-ones value and returns. Nothing else in the body is touched.

name: dispatch_sequence_commands_with_table
description: Sequence command reader in which one command type loads a pointer from a table and jumps into the shared fetch path. The other command values follow the same low-nibble dispatch and record updates as the neighbouring readers.

name: load_eight_words_from_table
description: Reads eight 16-bit words from a record pointed to by the caller's frame. A sentinel first word jumps to a routine chosen from a table, otherwise each word is stored and, when nonnegative, a pointer is looked up by its high byte and an associated counter and flag are reset.

name: clear_frame_byte_flag
description: Clears one byte in the caller's frame and returns. The facts report 76 instructions, but only this single store is visible in the decompiled body.

name: clear_frame_byte_flag
description: Clears one byte in the caller's frame and returns. The body is a single store with no other effects.

name: advance_channel_modulation_tick
description: Advances per-channel modulation once per tick: it counts down timers, adds a step to a running value and reverses that step when a count reaches zero, then writes a scaled level to an output word. Three unnamed helper calls run first.

name: update_channel_slide_and_output
description: Per-channel tick that counts a delay down and calls a table-selected routine when it expires. It adds a step to a running value, slides a target value toward the current value at a set rate, and writes the scaled value to an output word.

name: update_channel_slide_or_dispatch
description: Per-channel tick that sets a flag bit in a frame word and clears a record flag. When the frame flag is zero it calls a table-selected routine, otherwise it runs the same step and slide logic as its neighbours and writes the output word.

name: copy_record_value_and_dispatch
description: Copies a stored word from the record into a shared word, sets a flag byte from the caller's frame, advances a position counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: store_sum_and_dispatch_next
description: Clears a record byte, adds two frame values into a stored position word, writes the result to the output pointer, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: store_word_and_dispatch_next
description: Stores a word from the caller's frame into two record words, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: update_channel_slide_with_gate
description: Per-channel tick that uses a gate byte: when the gate is zero it sets the gate and calls a table-selected routine, otherwise it runs the step and slide logic and writes the output word.

name: update_countdown_and_dispatch
description: Updates a countdown byte in the record, either setting it to the all-ones value or decrementing it from a frame value. It then advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: advance_channel_slide_without_dispatch
description: Per-channel tick that clears a record byte and runs the timed step and slide logic, then writes the scaled value to an output word. It does not call a table-selected routine.

name: set_channel_pitch_from_table
description: Looks up a word in a 64-entry table indexed by a record byte plus a frame byte, scales it by a frame value and stores it as the channel's target. It then either dispatches through a table or runs the step and slide tick and writes the output word.

name: lookup_channel_value_from_table
description: Looks up a word in a 64-entry table indexed by a frame byte, scales it by a record value and stores it as the channel's target. It then either dispatches through a table or runs the step and slide tick and writes the output word.

name: set_envelope_params_and_dispatch
description: Stores a frame byte and a shifted copy of it into the record, sets an enable byte, and resets two record fields when the period field is zero. It then advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: compute_scaled_offset_and_dispatch
description: Stores a byte equal to a frame value plus three times a record value, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: store_byte_and_dispatch_next
description: Stores a frame byte into a record byte, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: store_four_bytes_and_dispatch
description: Stores four frame bytes into four record bytes, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: update_repeat_counter_and_dispatch
description: Updates a repeat counter in the record: it is set to idle, decremented, or reloaded from a frame value depending on its state. It then advances the command position and calls a table-selected routine.

name: advance_channel_slide_with_repeat
description: Per-channel tick that handles a repeat counter, a delay countdown and the timed step and slide logic, then writes the scaled value to an output word. Pending repeat state is cleared before the command dispatch continues.

name: select_record_table_and_dispatch
description: Saves the current position and counter fields, selects a pointer by indexing a table with a frame byte, sets the record counter from a frame word and calls a table-selected routine.

name: accumulate_offset_and_dispatch
description: Adds a frame longword into a position accumulator, writes it to an output pointer, reduces a level word by a shifted frame value, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: reset_position_and_dispatch
description: Clears a flag byte, sets the position accumulator from a frame longword, writes it to an output pointer, sets two output words to one, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: run_channel_tick_slide_gate
description: Per-channel tick that uses a gate byte and counter reload like its neighbours, runs the timed step and slide logic, then writes the scaled value to an output word.

name: advance_channel_tick_dma_flags
description: Per-channel tick that counts timers, steps and slides a value, and writes the scaled result to an output word, using the same logic as its neighbours. The facts also list interrupt and DMA control register accesses that do not appear in the decompiled body.

name: set_position_step_and_dispatch
description: Stores a frame byte into a record byte and a frame word as a position step, adds the step to a position accumulator, writes the accumulator to an output pointer, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: compare_table_byte_and_dispatch
description: Compares a frame byte with a byte read from memory at an address given by a frame word, advances the command counter by two on a match or by one otherwise, and calls a table-selected routine.

name: run_channel_tick_interrupt_gate
description: Per-channel tick that tests a gate byte in the record and calls a table-selected routine when it is clear, otherwise it runs the timed step and slide logic and writes the output word. The facts list an interrupt enable register write that the decompiled body does not show.

name: select_voice_record_and_countdown
description: Picks one of three fixed voice records by testing bit flags in a shared word, copies a field from that record into a shared word, and decrements the record's countdown. When the countdown goes negative it marks the record idle and reloads the shared word.

name: dispatch_or_jump_on_compare
description: Compares a frame byte with a record byte: if the frame byte is smaller it sets the command counter from a frame word, otherwise it increments the counter, then calls a table-selected routine.

name: reload_repeat_counter_and_dispatch
description: Decrements or reloads a repeat counter in the record, sets the command position from a frame word, and calls a table-selected routine. When the counter is idle it is set to the all-ones value first.

name: set_idle_and_dispatch_next
description: Sets a status byte in the record to the all-ones value, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: set_countdown_and_dispatch
description: Stores a frame byte minus one as a countdown in the record, sets the command position from a frame word and calls a table-selected routine.

name: step_repeat_counter_and_dispatch
description: Steps a repeat counter in the record, reloading it from a frame value when it expires, sets the command position from a frame word and calls a table-selected routine. The idle value is written first when the counter is clear.

name: store_frame_byte_and_dispatch
description: Stores a frame byte into a record byte, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: update_channel_pitch_slide_tick
description: Looks up a word in a 64-entry table indexed by a frame byte, scales it by a record value and runs the gate, timed step and slide logic. The result is written to an output word.

name: set_channel_target_and_dispatch
description: Stores a frame word as the channel's target value, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: clear_channel_state_and_dispatch
description: Clears a few record bytes and a target word, advances a counter and calls a table-selected routine.

name: select_record_table_and_dispatch
description: Saves the current position and counter fields, selects a pointer by indexing a table with a frame byte masked to seven bits, sets the record counter and calls a table-selected routine. The facts list 145 instructions, but the decompiled body is this short selection.

name: decode_channel_note_command
description: Decodes a command byte stored in a channel record: a special marker sets a gate counter, and negative values choose one of several setup branches that store bytes or table-based words. Values above a threshold look up a 64-entry word table, and ordinary values store the value and reset several record fields.

name: update_channel_entry_by_priority
description: Reads a four-byte entry from a table indexed by a frame word and selects a record by the low nibble of the entry's first byte. The entry is copied into that record only when the record is unset or its stored level is at or below the new level, and the level and companion word are updated.

name: clear_frame_byte_and_longword
description: Clears one byte in the caller's frame and a longword at a fixed offset from it, then returns.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes as a few stores of zero and constants with repeated calls to an unnamed routine, which looks like data misread as code. The facts list audio volume and DMA control register references, but the decompiled body only clears state words.

name: set_shared_word_and_call
description: Stores the input word into a shared word with one flag bit set, then calls an unnamed routine and returns.

name: initialise_channel_state_tables
description: Clears the channel's flags and counters, copies four words from a table indexed by a record byte into shared words, and resets an eight-entry table of pointers and constants. It then sets a shared control bit and marks the channel ready; the facts also list audio control and CIA port A register accesses.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code could be produced for this nine-instruction routine. The facts show only one unnamed call and entry from outside the static flow, so no behaviour is recovered.

name: return_all_ones_status
description: Returns the all-ones value in the full 32-bit width and does nothing else.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoded as bad instruction data that the decompiler truncated at once, so no behaviour can be recovered from this block.

name: setup_boot_block_exec_calls
description: Boot block entry routine of about 50 instructions for which no pseudo-code is available. The facts show calls into the exec library for memory allocation, interrupt disabling, I/O requests and supervisor state, plus reads of DMA and interrupt enable registers.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code is available for this 76-instruction boot block routine. The facts show one caller and one unnamed call, so only that call relationship is recovered.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code is available for this five-instruction boot block routine. The facts show only that it is called by one unnamed routine, so no behaviour is recovered.

name: issue_exec_doio_request
description: Calls the exec library I/O request routine through a library offset and writes an interrupt enable register. The routine has 21 instructions and two unnamed callers, and no pseudo-code is available.

name: pass_through_stack_value
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then returns the stack slot it was given unchanged.

name: expand_packed_entry_table
description: Waits through a short count-down delay, then rebuilds a table of 289 entries from packed source records. Each record gives a repeat count and a value, and the routine writes expanded bytes and a running offset for each entry, using a second lookup table.

name: expand_packed_entry_table
description: Rebuilds a table of 289 entries from packed source records, writing expanded bytes and a running offset for each entry. Each record gives a repeat count and a value, and entries without a matching record are zeroed.

name: continue_packed_entry_expansion
description: Continues the packed table expansion loop: it writes one expanded entry at a time from the current record, advances the running offset and moves to the next record when the repeat count runs out. It stops when the table end is reached.

name: expand_packed_entry_table
description: Entry point of the packed table expansion: it writes a zero entry, then walks source records, writing repeat-expanded entries and running offsets until the end of the 289-entry table. It uses the same expansion logic as its neighbours.

name: verify_checksum_then_init_state
description: XOR-sums 118 longwords from a fixed block and compares the result with a constant. On a mismatch it loops forever writing zeros upward through memory, otherwise it initialises several state fields and steps through a sequence of unnamed calls and count-down loops.

name: init_state_and_run_sequence
description: Initialises several state fields and then runs a sequence of calls to an unnamed routine, with count-down loops and step increments up to a limit. It clears the state flags at the end.

name: advance_step_and_run_sequence
description: Advances a step counter by eight and, when it reaches the boundary, increments a row counter and resets the step positions. It then runs the same count-down and call sequence as its neighbours before clearing the state flags.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine four times in a row and returns.

name: call_routine_three_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine three times in a row and returns.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine four times in a row and returns.

name: fill_table_with_pseudorandom_words
description: Waits briefly, then fills a buffer in repeated passes with a generated 16-bit sequence. Each word is produced from the previous value by a multiply-and-add step and XORed with its high byte, and passes repeat until a flag bit is set or a counter runs out.

name: fill_pseudorandom_table_cia
description: Makes a call to an unnamed routine and then performs the same pseudo-random word fill as its neighbour. The facts also list CIA port A and B register reads for joystick and disk status.

name: blend_pseudorandom_mask_into_buffer
description: Waits briefly and calls an unnamed routine three times, then repeatedly merges a table of words into a buffer across 40 rows of four words. Each word is combined with an existing buffer value and a generated pseudo-random mask, and passes repeat until a counter runs out.

name: stub_zero_fill_forever
description: Writes zero longwords upward from its own address in an endless loop. The facts show one unnamed call, but the body contains only the endless zeroing loop.

name: blend_pseudorandom_mask_cia
description: Makes two unnamed calls and then performs the same pseudo-random masked merge as its neighbour. The facts also list CIA port A and B register reads for joystick and disk status.

name: call_routine_twice
description: Calls one unnamed routine twice and returns.

name: mask_buffer_with_word_table
description: ANDs each word of a 40-row buffer with the matching word of a source table, four words per row, and applies the same operation across four regions at fixed offsets.

name: clear_eight_words_after_delay
description: Waits briefly, then clears eight consecutive words starting at a fixed record offset.

name: clear_eight_words_at_offset
description: Clears eight consecutive words starting at a fixed record offset and returns.

name: write_bit_column_to_buffers
description: Writes one column of bits into three buffers at a computed offset. For each of four rows it clears one bit position and sets it from the input byte, shifting the input one bit per row.

name: build_pointer_table_copy_state
description: Fills a four-entry table with addresses stepping by a fixed plane stride and stores a base pointer. It then copies 58 longwords from a shared block into the destination and copies nine words into a second area.

name: toggle_saved_value_flag
description: If a counter field is nonzero, copies a saved value back into the working field and clears the flag. Otherwise it saves the working value and sets the flag.

name: setup_vertical_interrupt_vector
description: Initialises an interrupt-related record and, when an argument is given, stores pointers into an interrupt vector slot and sets a shared word; without an argument it calls a library function through a vector. The text 'xenon vert int' is referenced, which suggests the vertical interrupt handler.

name: test_flag_and_call_handler
description: Tests a flag bit in a shared word and calls a fixed routine plus another unnamed routine when it is clear, or stores the flag word and calls a function pointer from a vector record when it is set. An interrupt request register and a custom chip register appear in the facts.

name: read_joystick_direction_state
description: Reads the mouse and joystick port movement registers and the CIA fire-button register, turns the direction bits into a stored state byte with a repeat delay, and writes a copper list pointer register. Two unnamed routines process the stored state afterwards.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Body is only a return with no other effect. The routine is called once from one unnamed routine.

name: wait_for_byte_change
description: Spins on a comparison of a record byte with itself, so the loop only ends if hardware changes that byte between reads. Returns its input value unchanged.

name: call_routine_count_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine once for each step of a count taken from the low word of its input, counting down to zero, then returns the input value.

name: store_cia_port_reading
description: Stores a 16-bit value built from two CIA port registers into a record field and returns the input unchanged. The facts list CIA port A and B register accesses.

name: generate_scaled_random_value
description: Advances a 16-bit pseudo-random state in a record field with a multiply-and-add step, replacing a zero state with one, then maps the result into a range from two inputs by division. The facts also list 16 calls and text references that the pseudo-code does not show.

name: append_byte_until_buffer_full
description: When a record flag is set, appends the input byte to a buffer and advances the buffer pointer and a counter. At a fixed limit of 650 entries it writes a terminator byte and calls several unnamed routines.

name: run_main_state_machine_loop
description: Main loop over a state byte that reads input, dispatches through a table of handler routines and updates position and timer fields each pass. Referenced text includes 'PRESS FIRE TO PLAY' and a data file name, and the facts record comparisons with executable hunk type codes, so loading or relocation code may be included.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Body is only a return with no other effect, and the routine is called once from one unnamed routine.

name: set_record_flag_bits_return
description: Writes a record byte back unchanged, ORs a set of bit flags into another record byte, and returns the input byte with its low six bits set.

name: return_constant_four
description: Returns the constant four and does nothing else.

name: copy_words_into_fixed_area
description: Copies 512 words from a buffer into a fixed record area and moves the old contents of that area into a second buffer. One record word is cleared first.

name: toggle_word_buffer_copy_direction
description: Flips a parity word in the record, then copies 512 words between a fixed record area and one of two buffers, choosing the copy direction from the parity.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns.

name: setup_blitter_copy_operation
description: Sets the blitter's mask, modulo, pointer, control and size registers for a copy-style operation over a block offset from the record, then returns. The facts also list a DMA control read.

name: advance_cell_frames_copy_blocks
description: Counts down a timer for each cell in a table and, when it expires, advances the cell's frame index. It copies an 8-word image block from a frame table into three buffers at fixed plane offsets, then updates two counters and calls unnamed routines when they change.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine four times in a row and returns.

name: sync_shadow_bytes_and_call
description: For each of two byte pairs, copies the source byte into a shadow byte when they differ and calls an unnamed routine after each change.

name: call_routine_sequence_five
description: Calls one unnamed routine twice with pairs of constant arguments, then three more times with no arguments, and returns.

name: call_routine_five_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine five times in a row and returns.

name: clamp_level_and_trigger_timer
description: Adds the input byte to a record level byte and clamps the result to a fixed range, calling a table-selected routine, setting a timer byte and storing the floor value when the level drops below zero. It does nothing while the record's gate flags are set.

name: sync_nine_bytes_tick_timers
description: Copies nine bytes from one record area to a mirror area, calling three unnamed routines for each byte that changes. It then counts down two timer words and calls an unnamed routine every 32nd tick.

name: print_decimal_digits_of_value
description: Converts a 32-bit value into decimal digits by repeated subtraction of descending powers of ten starting at 100000. It calls an unnamed routine for each digit it emits and suppresses leading zeros.

name: print_decimal_digits_from_record
description: Converts a value held in a record field into decimal digits by repeated subtraction of descending powers of ten starting at 100000. It calls an unnamed routine for each digit and one more time at the end.

name: convert_char_digit_and_emit
description: Subtracts the character code for zero from its input, optionally maps the result through a table, and calls one of two unnamed routines depending on whether the result is the newline or vertical tab code.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns.

name: emit_text_skipping_carriage_returns
description: Walks a zero-terminated text string and passes every character other than the carriage-return code to an unnamed routine. The walk ends at the terminator.

name: emit_text_skipping_carriage_returns
description: Same zero-terminated text walk as its neighbour: characters other than carriage return go to an unnamed routine, and the loop ends at the terminator.

name: render_cell_sequence_frames
description: Clears a block of record words, then computes plane addresses for each cell from a frame index and copies cell data into them while walking a table of per-cell command records. The facts list eight calls, and the routine is long enough that only part of its behaviour is visible here.

name: blit_rows_with_stride
description: Programs the blitter with fixed masks and modulo values, then runs 169 blit operations that each copy a block taken from a table, waiting for the blitter between them. The facts list blitter and DMA control register accesses.

name: blit_four_rows_unless_flagged
description: Unless a record flag equals one, programs the blitter with fixed masks and performs four blit operations, each advancing down by one plane stride. It waits for the blitter between operations.

name: blit_four_rows_unless_other
description: Same four-row blit as its neighbour, but guarded by a different record byte value.

name: call_routine_once
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns.

name: trap_if_flag_call_three
description: If a shared word is nonzero, raises a trap instruction. Then it calls three unnamed routines.

name: blit_copy_four_rows_pairs
description: Programs the blitter for a copy and runs four operations, each taking a pair of source and destination pointers that advance by one plane stride per row. It waits for the blitter after each operation.

name: call_routine_once
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns.

name: blit_clear_rows_with_stride
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then programs the blitter to write a fixed pattern across 192 rows, advancing 40 bytes per row and waiting for the blitter after each write.

name: fill_longs_with_all_ones
description: Fills 2240 longwords starting at a fixed record offset with the all-ones value and returns.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns.

name: blit_clear_fifty_six_rows
description: Programs the blitter to clear 56 rows at a fixed record offset, advancing 40 bytes per row and waiting for the blitter after each write.

name: return_input_unchanged
description: Returns its input value unchanged and does nothing else.

name: scan_neighbour_cells_and_clear
description: Scans four neighbouring positions taken from a direction table and tests the grid cell at each one. It calls unnamed routines for cells inside the fixed range that pass a check, then clears two record bytes.

name: scan_neighbour_cells_from_input
description: Scans four neighbouring grid positions, offset by the input values, and calls unnamed routines for each in-range cell that passes a check. It clears two record bytes when the scan ends.

name: scan_neighbour_cells_stepwise
description: Steps through four grid positions from a direction table, calling unnamed routines for in-range cells that pass a check. It clears two record bytes when it finishes.

name: scan_neighbour_cells_variant
description: Steps through grid positions from a direction table in the same way as its neighbours, calling unnamed routines for in-range cells that pass a check. It clears two record bytes at the end.

name: clear_two_record_bytes
description: Clears two consecutive bytes in the record and returns.

name: store_three_record_bytes
description: Stores three input register values into three record bytes and returns.

name: reset_state_and_copy_positions
description: Sets a counter word to six, sets a state flag and a timer byte, then copies two saved position words into their working fields.

name: clear_flag_and_restore_positions
description: Clears a flag byte and a timer byte, then copies two saved position words back into their working fields. The facts also note comparisons with executable hunk type codes, which the body does not show.

name: update_position_list_entries
description: Chooses an index value from a record field and calls an unnamed routine with it. When a flag is set it calls another unnamed routine and writes positions into 11-word list entries computed from record fields, clamping them to a maximum of 198.

name: blit_sprite_column_when_active
description: When a record state byte has one specific value, draws a column of blocks with the blitter using masks, modulo values and a source chosen from record position fields. Otherwise it stores a fixed default value in a record word, and one unnamed routine is called.

name: set_flag_bit_and_call
description: Sets the low bit of a record flag byte, calls one unnamed routine and returns.

name: blit_sprite_column_from_input
description: Draws a column of blocks with the blitter like its neighbour, using an input pointer for the source and a record flag to choose between two blitter control words. It waits for the blitter at several points.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code is available for this 147-instruction routine. The facts show a jump-table entry call, four unnamed calls and four unnamed callers, and nothing else is recovered.

name: allocate_list_slot_and_fill
description: Finds the first free 11-word entry in a list by scanning for a clear flag bit, zeroes it and fills its fields from a table indexed by the input. Entries with a secondary flag are drawn through a loop of unnamed calls, while the others store the input position values directly.

name: call_routine_then_mark_slot
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then writes the all-ones value into a byte of the record selected by an index byte.

name: allocate_list_slot_alt_base
description: Same first-free list slot allocation and fill pattern as its neighbour, but with a different list base and scan limit.

name: allocate_list_slot_third_base
description: Same list-slot allocation and fill as its neighbours, but with another list base and a scan limit of 59 entries.

name: clear_record_bytes_block
description: Clears 2200 bytes starting at a pointer held in a record field.

name: call_routine_for_inactive_slots
description: Walks 60 list slots at a 22-byte stride and, for each slot whose flag bit is clear, calls one unnamed routine. Returns the input value unchanged afterwards.

name: call_routine_for_active_slots
description: Walks 60 list slots at a 22-byte stride and, for each slot whose flag bit is set, calls one unnamed routine. Returns the input value unchanged afterwards.

name: call_routine_until_marker
description: Calls one unnamed routine repeatedly until it returns the letter X.

name: call_routine_until_bracket
description: Calls one unnamed routine repeatedly until it returns an open-bracket character.

name: tick_slot_counter_and_flag
description: Clears a slot's flag bit, looks up a step from a table by slot index and decrements the slot's counter. When the counter reaches zero it calls an unnamed routine if a flag is set, then adds a computed value to an accumulator and sets a pending flag.

name: write_slot_table_entries
description: If the top bit of a source word is clear, counts the used list entries and writes one table byte per slot from a lookup table, repeating over its length. Otherwise it calls an unnamed routine and writes the all-ones marker byte.

name: queue_three_blit_rows
description: Builds a blitter request at a record base, setting control and mask words from a flag, then waits for the blitter to be free before writing three row requests that each advance by a fixed plane stride. Calls two unnamed routines.

name: blit_clipped_sprite_row
description: Sets a shared flag bit, computes a row and column from the inputs, and when the row falls inside a 15-row window programs the blitter with masks, control words and modulo values to draw a clipped row of blocks at a computed address.

name: blit_clipped_row_with_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine to obtain a value, then draws a clipped row of blocks with the blitter in the same way as its neighbour.

name: blit_clipped_sprite_row_unflagged
description: Like its neighbours, draws a clipped row of blocks with the blitter at a computed address, but clears the shared flag bit first and writes the source pointer directly.

name: blit_clipped_sprite_block_rows
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then draws a clipped block of rows with the blitter, issuing three plane-strided blit requests per row like its neighbours.

name: register_table_slot_and_blit
description: Looks up the input value in a table of 31 longword slots, storing it in the first empty slot if it is absent. It then programs the blitter with fixed control and modulo values and performs a fill-style blit at an offset derived from the slot index.

name: clear_shared_word
description: Clears one shared word and returns. The facts list an audio channel 3 volume register, which the body does not write directly.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code is available for this 170-instruction routine. The facts show DMA control register accesses, four unnamed callers and one unnamed call, and nothing else is recovered.

name: step_audio_channel_sequences
description: Reads command bytes from a per-channel sequence stream, where some ranges set stream or table pointers or dispatch through a table and others update the channel's period and volume from a lookup table. For each channel it sets the matching DMA enable bits and calls unnamed routines to write the outputs.

name: step_audio_channel_from_input
description: Same command-stream sequencer as its neighbour, but the stream and starting values come from an input pointer. The first two bytes set the channel's initial state before the loop runs.

name: run_audio_channel_update_loop
description: Runs the per-channel sequencer loop without the initial setup. It sets the DMA enable bit for each channel, applies period and volume slides from a lookup table, and writes the results before calling unnamed routines.

name: step_audio_channel_setup_b
description: Same sequencer as its neighbours, starting from an input pointer and clearing a flag byte before the first command is read.

name: shift_noise_bit_register
description: Shifts one bit derived from a status value into a 16-bit shift register and a second shared word, then returns four times the computed value. The facts list disk and serial data register accesses, which the body does not show.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoded as bad instruction data that the decompiler truncated, so only a counter decrement and a DMA control write are visible.

name: write_copper_list_words
description: Calls two routines through a table, then writes a long series of words to a fixed copper-list address, each followed by a call to an unnamed routine. It also writes DMA control values and loops 15 times over a block of register pairs before calling a routine through a global pointer.

name: stub_decompiler_timed_out
description: No pseudo-code is available for this 25-instruction routine. The facts show one unnamed caller and four unnamed calls, and nothing else is recovered.

name: patch_jump_and_call_sites
description: Writes absolute jump instructions at three fixed addresses and absolute call instructions at seventeen more, each pointing at an unnamed routine. It also writes two no-op words and calls three unnamed routines before returning.

name: check_marker_then_patch_call
description: If a shared word equals a fixed marker value, writes an absolute call instruction with a routine pointer into a fixed address and calls a routine through a stored pointer. It then clears the shared word and returns it.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Body is only a return with no other effect.

name: replace_matching_words_in_range
description: Walks a range of words and replaces every word equal to the first input with the second input, stepping two bytes at a time until the end of the range.

name: fill_words_until_key_match
description: Writes a value into a word, then skips forward in steps of two bytes until it finds a word equal to a key or reaches the end of the range, repeating the write each time it finds one.

name: return_input_unchanged
description: Returns its input value unchanged and does nothing else.

name: call_routine_then_store_word
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the low word of the second input value into the location given by an address register.

name: set_flag_and_spin_forever
description: Sets a record byte to one and then enters an endless loop. The facts list a vertical position counter read, which the body does not show.

name: call_routine_then_store_word
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then stores the input word through a second address register.

name: store_routine_result_at_offset
description: Calls one unnamed routine that returns a value and stores the result as a word at a fixed offset from an address register.

name: call_then_store_d1_word
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then stores the second input word at a fixed offset from an address register.

name: call_then_store_d7_word
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then stores the seventh input word at a fixed offset from an address register.

name: wait_for_global_flag_clear
description: Spins while a shared word has the value-64 bit set, then returns. The facts list a DMA control register read, and the body does not modify any register or memory.

name: wait_for_global_flag_clear
description: Spins while a shared word has the value-64 bit set, then returns. It does not modify any registers or memory.

name: patch_call_site_and_jump
description: Sets a shared word to one and writes several constant opcode words and an absolute call instruction at fixed code addresses. It then calls a routine through a stored pointer and returns.

name: read_save_file_chunk
description: Calls a routine through a stored pointer to read up to 512 bytes into a shared buffer, then passes the count, capped at 512, to a second routine when any bytes were read. The text 'spcrus.sav' is referenced, which suggests a save file read.
